messages.subject: Errors during obsCovs creation
parts:
Hi all,
I'm working with unmarked for the first time and, as I have supposed, I'm occurring in a lot of errors. I have solved some of these, but I don't understand why pcount give me back an error when I choose some variables.
I have 240 sites that I have surveyed some once and some during four visits; I also have both several variables that I have recorded during each visit and some that I have recorded only one time (they describe the sites structure).
So, I have a dataset in which the sites are on rows and covariates are on columns (4 columns for repeated variables and only 1 column for site structure variables).
In order to create the model object, I'm using this script and it works

y1 <- dispar_1gen[,c(2:5)]       #surveying variable
time1 <- matrix(rep(as.character(1:4), nrow(y1)), ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE)
sc1 <- data.frame(f.erb=scale(dispar_1gen$f.erbosa), d.alb=scale(dispar_1gen$dis.alberi), hab=hab, zona=zona, row.names = dispar_1gen$Id.site)    #site variables. r, ac, af, tt
obsc1 <- list(r=r, rf=rf, ac=ac, af=af, tt=tt, hb=hb, time=time1) #observation variables

umf_1gen <- unmarkedFramePCount(y = y1,
                           siteCovs=sc1,
                           obsCovs=obsc1)

After this, I try to run the model using the following script

dm1.2 <- pcount(~ rf + hb ~ unlist(ac) + zona, data=umf_1gen, control=list(trace=TRUE, REPORT=5), mixture = c("P"))

and it give me back this error.....

Error in model.frame.default(stateformula, siteCovs, na.action = NULL) : 

  variable lengths differ (found for 'zona')



If I check the object structure, I can't see anything strange





Could someone help me??? please!!!!

Michele

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Errors during obsCovs creation
parts:
I think this is happening because you are trying to include an observation covariate (ac) with length 960 (240 x 4) in your state model, which is expecting a covariate with length equal to the number of sites (240). It also might be that calling `unlist(ac)` in the state formula is silently breaking and resulting in an empty column, which then cannot be combined with a `zona`, a  site covariate with length 240. Does the model run if you remove `unlist(ac)` from the formula? Can you summarize `ac` so that it has one value per site and put it in the siteCovs, and then change your call to 

dm1.2 <- pcount(~ rf + hb ~ ac + zona, data=umf_1gen, control=list(trace=TRUE, REPORT=5), mixture = c("P"))

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Errors during obsCovs creation
parts:
Michele,

There are various potential reasons for the error messages that are hard to sort out without having all the data and code to test. However, I think they are all related to a larger issue:

If you don't have a way of summarizing `ac` so that there is a single value for each site (thus yielding a vector of length 240), then you can't include it in your siteCovs (sc1) and you also can't include it in your state formula (the second part of the formula currently `~ac + zona`. The pcount model assumes that the true abundance is constant across your repeated visits, so it doesn't make sense to try to model abundance as a function of a covariate that changes between visits, as `ac` does. You can include `ac` in the obsCovs, and the detection formula (the first part of the formula currently `~rf + hb`) because detection probability can vary between visits.

If you completely remove ac from both the siteCovs (sc1) and your state formula (so your new formula would be ~rf+hb ~ zona) does the model run?

Ken
